"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, maintains, reads, and recites this Prajñāpāramitā, such a person will constantly utter speech that is faithful and compliant, gentle, pure, and unadulterated; they will not give rise to anger, will not be shrouded by pride, and will constantly generate a mind of loving-kindness;
they will not give rise to afflictions such as resentment, malice, or fury, nor allow them to increase."
Those sons or daughters of good family should constantly reflect:
"For the sake of seeking unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I must not give rise to anger toward those things that cause harm or affliction."
"Why is this? If the dharma of anger arises, the sense faculties undergo transformation, and the signs of a well-disciplined and virtuous appearance are no longer harmonized.
Having formed this thought, he dwelt securely in right mindfulness.
Kauśika! Because those sons and daughters of good family receive, uphold, read, and recite the Prajñāpāramitā, they obtain such merits in this present life.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma (Shi Hu), Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, Holder of the Purple Robe, under Imperial Edict. Chapter Three, Part Two: The Merits of the Jewel Stūpa. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is rare, World-Honored One!
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of dedication, and they do not give rise to signs through an inflated mind.
The Buddha said, “So it is, so it is!”

Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, upholds, reads, and recites this Dharma-gate of the *prajñāpāramitā*, explains it themselves or causes others to explain it, and practices according to what has been taught—by the power of such merit, when entering an army formation, they will have no fear; they will be courageous, firm, and victorious over enemy forces, and even in all their movements—walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—they shall attain auspiciousness.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, maintains, reads, and recites this Prajñāpāramitā, that person will, in all places—whether walking or standing—encounter no harm from such dangers as blades or staves; even when their life is about to end, they shall give rise to no fear."

Why is this? This Prajñāpāramitā is the great illumination; this Prajñāpāramitā is the immeasurable illumination; this Prajñāpāramitā is the unsurpassed illumination; this Prajñāpāramitā is the unequaled illumination; this Prajñāpāramitā is the illumination equal to the unequaled.

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family practices and studies such a vidyā-mantra, they will not dwell upon their own evil, nor dwell upon the evil of others, nor dwell upon the evil of both themselves and others.
Kauśika! You should know that those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this *prajñāpāramitā* shall obtain such merits in the present life.

Furthermore, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva studies this vidyā, they are able to realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and achieve the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*). Because they have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they are able to observe and penetrate the various mental activities of all sentient beings.
That which is called "the knowledge of all modes" refers to all dharmas of clarity.

Among these, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is a student who is such that there is not the slightest dharma into which he cannot enter, not the slightest dharma which he cannot fully comprehend, and not the slightest dharma which he cannot realize.
Therefore, it is named the "knowledge of all-knowledge" (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Furthermore, Kauśika, if there is anyone who can write out this *prajñāpāramitā* as a scriptural volume and make offerings to it while upholding it, or if they personally recite it, or further encourage others to do so, even explaining its meaning for them, such a person will not be able to be taken advantage of by any humans or non-humans. They will be constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, except for the ripening of past karmic retributions.

Kauśika! For example, regarding the great site of enlightenment and the area surrounding the Bodhi tree in all its directions and corners, neither humans nor non-humans, nor even animals of various species, can enter, nor can they dwell there; they cannot destroy it or commit any evil against it.
Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present have realized the Buddha-bodhi at this very place.

Kauśika! It is likewise for good sons and good daughters who receive, uphold, read, recite, copy, and make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā; neither humans nor non-humans shall find an opportunity against them, nor shall they be able to destroy them or bring forth faults and evils.

Why is this? If one makes offerings at a place where this *Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* resides, that region shall be regarded as equivalent to having constructed various jeweled stūpas; it should be honored with offerings, venerated, and praised.
“Kauśika! You should know that this Prajñāpāramitā possesses such merits in the present life.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Bhagavān! If there are good sons or good daughters who write down this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra and honor it with respect, placing upon it various exquisite flowers, burning incense, unguents, powdered incense, and flower garlands, up to and including various exquisite banners and canopies, and lighting oil lamps—performing such various kinds of offerings as these.”

Furthermore, if there are sons or daughters of good family who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, collect his relics and erect a sublime jeweled stūpa, honoring, revering, gazing upon, and praising it, and making various offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, and precious canopies.
“Between the merit obtained by those sons and daughters of good family and the merit mentioned previously,
which is greater? The Buddha said, “Kauśika!
I now ask you; answer as you see fit. What do you think?
By training in what dharmas did the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha obtain such a body, realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and achieve the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

It is because the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has practiced and studied the Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā that he has realized anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and attained all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna).”
The Buddha said, “Kauśika!

Therefore you should know that it is not by means of this body that a Buddha attains the fruit of Tathāgatahood; rather, it is by accomplishing the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) that one becomes a Tathāgata.”

It should be known that all the wisdom of omniscience of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, arises from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā); furthermore, the body of the Tathāgata arises from the skillful means (upāyakauśalya) of the perfection of wisdom. Therefore, this body serves as the basis for the wisdom of omniscience.
Because they take the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) as their support, they attain the Buddha-body, the Dharma-body, and the Saṃgha-body.

Therefore, all sentient beings are able to behold, pay homage to, and make offerings to the body of the Tathāgata, and even after his parinirvāṇa, they erect stupas for the Buddha’s relics to make offerings to them.

Kauśika! Although those sons or daughters of good family may thus erect stupas and make offerings to the relics of the Tathāgata, it is not as meritorious as someone who writes out this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra and, with respect and reverence, makes various offerings to it—such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, and precious canopies.
These sons and daughters of good family will obtain exceedingly great merit.
Why is this? To make offerings to this *prajñāpāramitā* is to make offerings to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Therefore, sons and daughters of good family, if you wish to make offerings to those who possess all-encompassing wisdom, you should always transcribe, revere, uphold, and make various offerings to this Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

If the people of Jambudvīpa are unable to copy, receive, uphold, read, or recite this Prajñāpāramitā; if they do not proclaim it themselves nor cause others to proclaim it; and furthermore, if they are unable to respectfully make offerings to it with various incenses, flowers, banners, pennants, and precious canopies."
“World-Honored One!
Such persons as these have lost the great benefit of wholesome merit and will be unable to accomplish a vast karmic fruition.
The Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
“Kauśika! What do you think? How many people are there in Jambudvīpa who have attained indestructible faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha?”
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Among the people of this Jambudvīpa, those who have attained indestructible faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha are extremely few.”
The Buddha said, “Kauśika, it is so, it is so!”

Among the people of Jambudvīpa, there are few who are able to attain indestructible faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṃgha; those who have realized the fruit of a Srotāpanna, a Sakṛdāgāmin, an Anāgāmin, an Arhat, or the fruit of a Pratyekabuddha are likewise extremely rare.

Regarding this mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, those who have already resolved upon it are able to abide in non-retrogression; those currently resolving upon it are courageous and diligent; and those who have not yet resolved upon it will be able to do so—such persons are exceedingly rare.

Furthermore, among the people of Jambudvīpa, few are able to dwell in accordance with this Prajñāpāramitā; few are able to practice in reliance upon this Prajñāpāramitā according to the Dharma; few are able to abide in the stage of a bodhisattva with a non-retrogressive mind regarding this Prajñāpāramitā; and few are able to practice this Prajñāpāramitā and proceed toward the realization of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Kauśika! If there are those who can hear, receive, read, and recite this Prajñāpāramitā; whether they explain it themselves or cause others to explain it, practice according to its teaching, and even honor and revere it with various offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, and precious canopies—it should be known that all such persons have already resolved their minds toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and abide on the stage of non-retrogression of the bodhisattvas.

"Furthermore, Kauśika! Within this Jambudvīpa, there are immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings who have resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and practice the bodhisattva path."
What do you think, Kauśika?

You should now know that although there may be such immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings who resolve upon bodhicitta and practice the bodhisattva path, among them only one or two will abide in the stage of non-retrogression.

Why is this? Because there are sentient beings in this Jambudvīpa who give rise to inferior minds and conceive inferior thoughts; their wisdom, faith, and understanding are likewise inferior. For this reason, they exert inferior diligence, regarding Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi as something difficult to attain, and failing to give rise to the aspiration for it, they fall into indolence.

Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family desires to swiftly realize the fruit of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and achieve the supreme bliss, they should therefore give rise to a fierce and keen resolve toward this Prajñāpāramitā, listening to it, receiving it, reading it, and reciting it.
Why is this? These sons and daughters of good family should form this thought:
"When the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha was practicing the bodhisattva path in the past, he also studied in this way; I too now study this Prajñāpāramitā, and this Prajñāpāramitā is my teacher."
"Kauśika! Whether the Buddha remains in the world or has entered parinirvāṇa, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should rely upon this Prajñāpāramitā."
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If there are sons or daughters of good family who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, construct ten million stupas made of the seven precious substances from the Buddha’s relics, and for as long as they live, offer various kinds of worship such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious parasols, and exquisite garments, and furthermore honor, gaze upon, prostrate to, and praise them."
Kauśika! What do you think?
Would that son of good family or daughter of good family obtain much merit by reason of this offering?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to the Buddha:
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! If there are sons or daughters of good family who, desiring to seek great enlightenment, give rise to a mind of faith and understanding toward this Prajñāpāramitā, and themselves uphold, recite, read, and remember it, further explaining and disseminating it extensively for others so that all sentient beings may universally obtain great and wholesome benefit and the True Dharma may long abide in the world—[they shall be protected by me].”

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is uninterrupted and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the various assemblies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each uphold, proclaim, and expound it, they immediately attain the unimpaired and indestructible Dharma-eye.

Furthermore, one should transcribe this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra and place it in a pure location with a mind of reverence, making various kinds of offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments.
Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family will obtain exceedingly great merit. Furthermore, Kauśika!

Setting aside for a moment the previously mentioned number of *koṭi* of jeweled stupas, suppose there were someone who constructed stupas made of the seven precious substances out of the Buddha’s relics until they filled Jambudvīpa; and suppose that person, throughout the remainder of their life, were to offer various kinds of worship—such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments—and furthermore, were to honor, gaze upon, prostrate before, and praise them.
Kauśika! What do you think?
By this cause and condition, would that son of good family or daughter of good family acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to the Buddha,
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! If there are good sons or good daughters who, desiring to seek great enlightenment, give rise to a mind of faith and understanding toward this Prajñāpāramitā, and personally uphold, recite, memorize, and chant it, further extensively explaining and disseminating it for others so that all sentient beings may universally obtain great and wholesome benefit, and so that the True Dharma may long abide in the world.

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is not severed and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the various assemblies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each uphold, proclaim, and expound it, they immediately attain the Dharma-eye, which is indestructible and imperishable.

Furthermore, one should write out this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, place it in a pure location with a mind of reverence, and perform various kinds of offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments.
Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family will acquire exceedingly great merit. Furthermore, Kauśika!

Setting aside for a moment the previously mentioned construction of stūpas made of the seven precious substances filling Jambudvīpa, suppose there were a person who, with the relics of the Buddha, constructed stūpas made of the seven precious substances filling the four great continents.

Throughout their entire life, this person were to offer various kinds of worship—such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments—and furthermore, were to revere, gaze upon, prostrate before, and praise them.
Kauśika! What do you think? Would those sons or daughters of good family obtain much merit by reason of this?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to the Buddha,
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! If there are sons or daughters of good family who, desiring to seek great bodhi, give rise to a mind of faith and resolve toward this Prajñāpāramitā, and themselves uphold, recite, read, and remember it, further extensively explaining and disseminating it for others so that all sentient beings may universally attain great and wholesome benefit, and so that the True Dharma may long abide in the world.

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is uninterrupted and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each upholds, proclaims, and expounds it, they immediately attain the unimpaired and indestructible Dharma-eye.

Furthermore, one should transcribe this *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* and place it in a pure location with a mind of reverence, making various kinds of offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments.
Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family will acquire exceedingly great merit. Furthermore, Kauśika!
As previously described, let us set aside the case of one who constructs stūpas made of the seven precious jewels filling the four great continents. Kausika!

Suppose there were a person who, with the relics of the Buddha, constructs stūpas made of the seven precious jewels filling a small thousand-world system, and for as long as their life lasts, makes various kinds of offerings to them—such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, and precious parasols—and furthermore honors, gazes upon, prostrates to, and praises them.
Kauśika! What do you think? Would that person, by reason of these causes and conditions, acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to the Buddha,
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! If there are sons or daughters of good family who, desiring to seek great enlightenment, give rise to a mind of faith and understanding toward this Prajñāpāramitā, and themselves uphold, recite, and remember it, further explaining and disseminating it extensively for others so that all sentient beings may universally attain great and wholesome benefit, and so that the True Dharma may long abide in the world.

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is uninterrupted and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each upholds, proclaims, and expounds it, they immediately attain the Dharma-eye that is indestructible and imperishable.

Furthermore, one should write out this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra and place it in a pure location, making various kinds of offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments.
Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family will acquire exceedingly great merit. Furthermore, Kauśika!
As previously described, let us set aside the case of someone constructing stūpas made of the seven precious jewels filling a small thousand-world system. Kausika!

Suppose there were a person who, using the Buddha’s relics, constructed stūpas made of the seven precious jewels filling a medium thousand-world system, and throughout their entire life, offered various kinds of worship—such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments—and furthermore, honored, gazed upon, prostrated to, and praised them.
Kauśika! What do you think? Would that person, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to the Buddha,
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! If there are sons or daughters of good family who, desiring to seek great enlightenment, give rise to a mind of faith and understanding toward this Prajñāpāramitā, and themselves uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, further extensively explaining and disseminating it for others so that all sentient beings may universally obtain great and wholesome benefit, and cause the True Dharma to abide long in the world.

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is not severed and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the various assemblies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each uphold it, they immediately attain the indestructible and imperishable Dharma-eye.

Furthermore, one should write out this *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* and place it in a pure location, making various kinds of offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments.
Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family will obtain exceedingly great merit. Furthermore, Kauśika!
As previously described, let us set aside the case of someone constructing stūpas made of the seven precious substances filling a medium chiliocosm. Kausika!

Suppose there were a person who, with the relics of the Buddha, constructed stūpas made of the seven precious substances filling a great trichiliocosm; and suppose that for as long as their life lasted, they offered various kinds of worship—such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments—and furthermore, revered, gazed upon, prostrated before, and praised them.
Kauśika! What do you think? Would that person, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to the Buddha,
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! If there are sons or daughters of good family who, desiring to seek great enlightenment, give rise to a mind of faith and understanding toward this Prajñāpāramitā, and personally uphold, recite, read, and remember it, further explaining and disseminating it extensively for others so that all sentient beings may universally obtain great and wholesome benefit and the True Dharma may long abide in the world—[they shall do so].”

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is not severed and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the various assemblies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each receive and uphold it, they immediately attain the indestructible and imperishable Dharma-eye.

Furthermore, one should write out this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra and place it in a pure location, making various kinds of offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments.
Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family will obtain exceedingly great merit. Furthermore, Kauśika!
"Kauśika, let us set aside for now the aforementioned construction of stūpas made of the seven precious substances filling a trichiliocosm.

Suppose, Kauśika, that every sentient being within this trichiliocosm were each to construct a stūpa of the seven precious substances from the Buddha’s relics, and were to maintain them for an entire kalpa or slightly less than a kalpa, making vast offerings such as various perfumes, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments, even including all kinds of music, song, and dance; and furthermore, were to revere, gaze upon, prostrate to, and praise them."
Kauśika! What do you think? Would those sentient beings, by reason of this cause and condition, acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to the Buddha,
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, desiring to seek great enlightenment, should give rise to a mind of faith and understanding toward this Prajñāpāramitā, personally uphold, recite, read, and remember it, and further explain and disseminate it extensively for others so that the True Dharma may long abide in the world.”

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is not severed and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each receives and upholds it, they immediately attain the unimpaired and indestructible Dharma-eye.

Furthermore, one should write down this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra and place it in a pure location, making various kinds of offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, and precious canopies.
“Kauśika! You should know that these sons and daughters of good family will obtain exceedingly great merit.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One! It is so, it is so!
It is truly as the Buddha has said:

if a person honors and makes offerings to this *Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, one should know that such a person is identical to making offerings to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present; they realize the wisdom of all Buddhas and is identical to performing the most supreme and boundless offerings throughout all worlds.”
"Bhagavān! As for the trichiliocosm mentioned by the Buddha with its aforementioned number, I now set aside that number as well, Bhagavān!"

Suppose there were as many trichiliocosm world systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, and those worlds were filled with sentient beings; and suppose each and every sentient being were to erect a stupa made of the seven precious gems for the Buddha’s relics, maintaining it for an eon or slightly less than an eon, making offerings of various fragrant flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, jeweled canopies, exquisite garments, and even all kinds of music, song, and dance, while further honoring, prostrating to, and praising them.
World-Honored One!

Although those sentient beings may acquire much merit, it does not equal that of someone who, desiring to seek great bodhi, gives rise to a mind of faith and resolve toward this *prajñāpāramitā*, personally upholding, reciting, memorizing, and reflecting upon it, and further extensively expounding and disseminating it for others, so as to cause all sentient beings everywhere to obtain great and wholesome benefit and to ensure that the True Dharma abides long in the world.

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is not interrupted and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the various assemblies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each uphold it, they immediately attain the indestructible and imperishable Dharma-eye.

Furthermore, one should write out this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra and place it in a pure location, making various kinds of offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, pennants, precious canopies, and exquisite garments.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
“So it is, so it is! Kauśika!”

One who is able to honor and make offerings to this *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* should know that the merit they obtain will be immeasurable and incalculable, boundless and peerless, even to the point that such merit is inconceivable.

Why is this? One should know that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha’s omniscience arises from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and furthermore, the body of the Tathāgata arises from omniscience.
Kauśika! Therefore, you should know this:

if one person were to erect a stūpa for the relics of the Buddha and make offerings to it, and another were to receive, uphold, read, recite, revere, and make offerings to this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, then when comparing the meritorious conduct and the resulting virtues of these two, the former does not equal even a hundredth part of the latter; it does not equal a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a koṭi-th part; it does not equal a hundred-koṭi-th part, a thousand-koṭi-th part, a hundred-thousand-koṭi-th part, or a hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-th part. It does not equal a fraction, a calculation, a metaphor, or even an upaniṣad-part of the latter.
At that time, forty thousand sons of gods who had previously come to the assembly together with Śakra, Lord of the Devas, all addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
"We shall now receive, uphold, read, recite, memorize, contemplate, and practice according to the instructions this profound Dharma-gate of the Perfection of Wisdom."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
"Kauśika! Just as the devas have said, you should receive, uphold, read, recite, remember, contemplate, and practice according to the instructions this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā."
Why is this? Kausika!

If the asuras should engage in battle with the hosts of the thirty-three devas, at that time you should contemplate this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā; then those asuras will immediately retreat and vanish of their own accord.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This Prajñāpāramitā is a vast and great illumination; this Prajñāpāramitā is an immeasurable illumination, it is the unsurpassed illumination, it is the most supreme illumination, it is the unequaled illumination, and it is the illumination equal to the unequaled.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: "So it is, so it is! Kauśika!"

This Prajñāpāramitā is a vast illumination, an immeasurable illumination, an unsurpassed illumination, a most excellent illumination, an incomparable illumination, and an illumination equal to the unequaled.

Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present are born from this Great Illumination; because the Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi of all Buddhas is attained through training in this Great Illumination; and because even the Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi of the immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-Bhagavāns throughout the trichiliocosm is achieved by training in this vast Great Illumination of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Kauśika! You should know that anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi comes from this prajñāpāramitā;
all the dharmas of the ten wholesome paths appear in the world because of this Great Illumination.

The factors of the four dhyānas, the factors of the four immeasurables, the factors of the four formless attainments, the factors of the five supernormal powers, and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment—all such dharmas as these appear in the world because of this Great Illumination.
Thus, in brief, even the eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma all arise from the vast and great mantra syllables of the Prajñāpāramitā.
All Buddha-wisdom, spontaneous wisdom, and inconceivable wisdom likewise arise from this great illumination. Furthermore, Kauśika!

If a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha does not appear in the world, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have appeared in the world will, based on the Prajñāpāramitā they have previously heard, give rise to various skillful means and act for the benefit of all sentient beings out of compassion for the world.

Therefore, these dharmas—the ten wholesome paths of action, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the five supernormal powers, and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment—have appeared in the world to reveal them to sentient beings.
Kauśika! For example, when the moon does not appear, the various stars emerge and, according to their own power and influence, illuminate the world.
It is the same for the bodhisattva mahāsattva: when a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha does not appear in the world, the True Dharma does not vanish or perish.

Why is this? Because whether it be the practice of all dharmas, the practice of equanimity, or the practice of all virtues, each and every one of them is born from the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas; they proceed in accordance with the skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas.
One should know that these skillful means of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas all arise from the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Kauśika!

If there are sons or daughters of good family who are able, regarding this Dharma-door of the Prajñāpāramitā, to copy it, make offerings to it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, remember and contemplate it, and practice according to its teaching.
"By virtue of these conditions, this person shall obtain great benefit in the present life.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What benefit shall this person obtain in the present life? The Buddha said, "Kauśika!

It should be known that these sons and daughters of good family shall not have their lives harmed by various poisons, nor be burned by fire, nor drowned by water; they shall not encounter the suffering of swords, blades, or staffs, nor even have their lives harmed by the power of others, and furthermore, they shall not be subjected to the laws of kings.
Even if such difficulties should arise, if one can recite and contemplate the *prajñāpāramitā*, one will immediately attain liberation. Furthermore, Kauśika, if those who uphold, read,

and recite the *prajñāpāramitā* go before a king, his princes, or his ministers, those kings, ministers, and others will rejoice upon seeing them, and everything they desire will be fulfilled according to their wishes.
Why is this? Kauśika!

This Prajñāpāramitā is the practice of the mind of great loving-kindness and the practice of great loving-kindness for all sentient beings; it is the practice of the mind of great compassion and the practice of great compassion.
Furthermore, Kauśika!

Those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this Prajñāpāramitā will, in all places, not be harmed by any tigers, wolves, insects, or beasts; nor shall those such as humans or non-humans who seek out their faults find any opportunity to do so, except for those karmic results that must necessarily be experienced due to past actions.

At that time, there were various non-Buddhist practitioners who had long been ordained within their own traditions; numbering a full hundred, they entered the assembly with the intent to disturb and trouble the Blessed One.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saw from afar this person gradually approaching the assembly of the Buddha.
Immediately, the Lord observed his mind and, knowing his intent, thought to himself:
"These non-Buddhists have now come to the assembly of the Buddha wishing to cause disturbance."
"I have previously received the Dharma-gate of the Perfection of Wisdom from the Buddha; it is fitting that I should recite and contemplate it.
Having thought this, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, immediately recited the Dharma-gate of the Perfection of Wisdom.

When the various non-Buddhists had entered the assembly and saw the World-Honored One from afar, they each circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right and then departed from the Buddha’s assembly, returning by the way they had come.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra had this thought:
"Why have these various non-Buddhists entered the assembly, circumambulated the Buddha, the World-Honored One, to the right, and then withdrawn?"
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in Śāriputra’s mind, addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:

“You should now know that those various non-Buddhists, having each gone forth in their respective teachings, have now come to this assembly of the Buddha desiring to cause destruction, contention, and affliction.”
Because Śakra, Lord of the Devas, recited the Prajñāpāramitā, those non-Buddhists were naturally filled with shame and withdrew. Śāriputra!
Therefore, you should know that this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā possesses great majestic power, capable of eliminating all the evil views of non-Buddhists.
At that time, there were also hosts of evil Māras who all thought to themselves:
"Now the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with his fourfold assembly and the devaputras of the desire and form realms, has gathered in this assembly."
That Buddha, the World-Honored One, has bestowed the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi upon various Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas; we should now proceed to that place.
When the hosts of Māras had formed this thought, they immediately manifested the fourfold army, adorned in various ways, and proceeded to the place where the Buddha was.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saw these four armies, well-ordered and magnificent, entering the assembly of the Buddha.
He then thought to himself:

"This fourfold army, so magnificently adorned and beautiful, does not belong to King Bimbisāra, nor to King Prasenajit, nor to any other kings, nor even to this son of a householder; rather, it is because these are manifestations created by those evil Māras."

Why is this? Because those hosts of Māras, throughout the long night, have opposed the Buddha-dharma, seeking out its vulnerabilities with the intent to cause destruction; I should now recite the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā as received from the Buddha.
Having formed this thought, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, immediately recited the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Thereupon, those hosts of Māras each withdrew their emanations and returned by the way they had come.

At that time, the assembly of the thirty-three deva sons immediately manifested within the gathering countless celestial mandārava flowers and various other exquisite blossoms, scattering them over the Buddha.
The flowers they scattered remained suspended in mid-air.
Then, after the assembly of devaputras had scattered these exquisite flowers, they spoke these words:
"May this sublime Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā remain long in the world, bringing great benefit to the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa."
Having spoken these words, he again scattered flowers; having scattered them, he spoke once more:
"I only pray that all sentient beings will proclaim, expound, and practice according to the teachings this Dharma-door of the Prajñāpāramitā."
All Māras, celestial beings of the Māra realm, humans, and non-humans who seek out faults shall find no opportunity; they shall cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with roots of goodness.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are those who can rejoice in, listen to, and receive this Prajñāpāramitā, one should know that such persons have already made offerings to the Buddhas of the past; how much more so for those who uphold, read, recite, remember, contemplate, and explain its meaning to others, practicing according to the Dharma as it is taught, and achieving realization in accordance with their practice.”
Why is this? Because the all-knowledge of all Buddhas is sought within the dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā, for it is born from the Prajñāpāramitā.
“World-Honored One!
It is like a person who, desiring to seek exquisite jewels, must enter the great ocean and seek with diligent toil before finally obtaining priceless and wondrous treasures.”
In the same way, the jewel of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha’s omniscience should likewise be sought within the great ocean of the Prajñāpāramitā.
The Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:

"So it is, so it is! Those who wish to seek the jewel of the omniscience of all Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, should seek it with diligent effort within the great ocean of the Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā; those who seek in this manner shall all attain their wishes."

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma (Shi Hu), Imperially Appointed Grand Officer for Court Service, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, recipient of the purple robe, under imperial decree. Chapter Three, Part Three: On the Merits of the Jewel Stūpa. At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How is it, World-Honored One?”

Why is it that you do not praise and proclaim the names of the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, and the perfection of meditative concentration, but instead speak only of the perfection of wisdom and its meritorious qualities?
The Buddha said to Ānanda: “So it is, so it is!
Among all the pāramitās, I have spoken only of the Prajñāpāramitā as the most supreme and worthy of praise.”
Why is this? Ānanda! You should now know that this Prajñāpāramitā serves as the guide and leader for the five other pāramitās.
Ānanda! What do you think?
If one practices generosity without dedicating it toward all-knowledge, will it become a pāramitā?
Ānanda replied to the Buddha,
“No, World-Honored One! The Buddha said:
“Ānanda! If one practices ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration without dedicating them toward omniscience, will they become perfections (pāramitās)?”
"If this very prajñā were not dedicated toward omniscience, could it be established as a pāramitā?
Ānanda replied to the Buddha,
"No, World-Honored One!"
The Buddha said: "Ānanda, what do you think?"
"Are all these inconceivable roots of wisdom and merit dedicated toward omniscience?
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
"So it is, so it is! All roots of goodness of the most supreme and inconceivable wisdom are entirely dedicated toward omniscience.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Therefore, you should know that because all roots of goodness are dedicated toward omniscience, they receive the name 'perfections' (pāramitā);
because the dharma of the ultimate truth is dedicated toward omniscience, it receives the name 'perfection of wisdom' (prajñāpāramitā)."
Therefore, Ānanda, because those roots of goodness are dedicated toward omniscience, the perfection of wisdom serves as the leader of the five perfections.
Those five perfections abide within the dharmas associated with the perfection of wisdom; it is by virtue of this perfection of wisdom that all the perfections are brought to full completion.
Ānanda! For this reason, I most highly praise the Prajñāpāramitā.
It is like when various seeds are scattered upon the great earth; according to the time and place and through their respective combinations, each attains growth.
Just as those various seeds depend upon the earth to abide, and cannot grow if they do not depend upon the earth, so too is it with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā):

it is able to encompass those five perfections (pañca-pāramitā). These five dharmas all abide in dependence upon the perfection of wisdom and attain growth by means of the perfection of wisdom; therefore, these five dharmas are all designated as "perfections."
"Ānanda! For this reason, you should know that the Prajñāpāramitā serves as the leader of those five dharmas.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

As the Buddha has taught, this Dharma-gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* possesses great merit; even if a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha were to praise and extol it with various words and phrases, he could not exhaust its qualities.”
Therefore, all sons and daughters of good family should receive, uphold, read, recite, remember, contemplate, and practice according to the instructions this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā.
The Buddha said: “Kauśika, excellent, excellent!”
It is as you have said.

Regarding this Dharma-gate of the Perfection of Wisdom, I do not merely say that those who can receive, uphold, read, recite, proclaim, and expound it possess great merit; rather, if there are sons or daughters of good family who, by means of this Perfection of Wisdom, merely write out the scriptural volume and place it in a pure location, honoring and revering it with various incenses, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious parasols, and exquisite garments as offerings—you should know that such a person is proclaiming the Buddha-Dharma so that it may long abide in the world.

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is not severed and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each upholds it, they immediately attain the indestructible and imperishable Dharma-eye.
“Kauśika! Those who uphold, read, and recite this Prajñāpāramitā shall obtain these merits in this present life.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are good sons or good daughters who, being able to merely transcribe this *prajñāpāramitā* into a scroll and place it in a pure location, offer various incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, pennants, precious canopies, and so forth as offerings according to their means—I shall go there to protect and mindfully attend to that person, ensuring they are free from decline and affliction; how much more so for those who receive, uphold, read, recite, remember, contemplate, and explain its meaning to others. The merit of such a person is immeasurable and boundless.”
The Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: “Excellent, excellent, Kauśika!”

If there are sons or daughters of good family who, in various places, preach this Prajñāpāramitā, then countless hundreds of thousands of devaputras will go to those locations to hear the Dharma, in order to listen to and receive the true teaching.

If the Dharma-preacher should feel weary or have no desire to speak, those devaputras will augment his strength so that he does not falter, causing him to apply himself with diligence and joyfully desire to proclaim the teaching.
Kauśika! Those who uphold, recite, and study the Prajñāpāramitā shall obtain these merits in this present life. Furthermore, Kauśika!

If good sons or good daughters who uphold this True Dharma preach this Prajñāpāramitā among the fourfold assembly, their minds will be free from timidity and fear; they will not dread difficult questions, will be able to answer according to whatever is asked, and will remain free from all faults.
Why is this? Because they are protected by the power of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Those who seek to find fault with this *prajñāpāramitā* shall find no opportunity.
Why is this? Because this Prajñāpāramitā is free from all faults; therefore, one who proclaims the Prajñāpāramitā likewise does not perceive any fault in it.
For this reason, those sons and daughters of good family will not give rise to fear or alarm when the Dharma is being taught.
Kausika, those who receive,
uphold, read, and recite the Prajñāpāramitā shall obtain these merits in the present life.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, maintains, reads, and recites the Prajñāpāramitā, such a person will be respected and loved by their parents, friends, and relatives, and even by śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and others."
Whether they have already arisen or have not yet arisen, all matters of litigation, disputes, decline, and affliction will be entirely far removed.
Kausika, those who receive, uphold, read, and recite the Prajñāpāramitā shall obtain these merits in this present life.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to write out this Prajñāpāramitā as a manuscript and install it for veneration, then in whatever region this scripture is located, the hosts of devaputras from the Cāturmahārājika Heaven who abide in the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* will, out of reverence for the Dharma, go to that place to behold, worship, praise, rejoice in, and receive it upon their heads."
Having paid homage and received [the teaching] upon his head, he immediately returned to that heaven.

All the hosts of devaputras dwelling in the Heaven of the Thirty-three who abide in the bodhicitta, the hosts of devaputras dwelling in the Yāma Heaven who abide in the bodhicitta, the hosts of devaputras dwelling in the Tuṣita Heaven who abide in the bodhicitta, the hosts of devaputras dwelling in the Nirmāṇarati Heaven who abide in the bodhicitta, and the hosts of devaputras dwelling in the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven who abide in the bodhicitta—all such hosts of devaputras from the desire realm—each went to his location out of reverence for the Dharma, to pay homage, praise, rejoice in, and receive it upon their heads.
Having obtained the opportunity to gaze upon him, pay homage, and receive his teachings, they each returned to their respective heavens. "Furthermore, Kauśika!
As for all the gods of the form realm (rūpadhātu), namely:"

The gods of the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Mahābrahmā, Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, Ābhāsvara, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Śubhakṛtsna, Anabhraka, Puṇyaprasava, Bṛhatphala, Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha—heavenly hosts among these various deities who dwell with the bodhicitta went to that place out of reverence for the Dharma; there they paid homage, praised it, rejoiced in it, and received it upon their heads.
Having obtained the opportunity to behold, pay homage to, and receive [the teaching] upon their heads,
they each returned to their respective celestial realms. "Furthermore, Kauśika,
those sons of good family and daughters of good family who uphold, read, and recite the Prajñāpāramitā should give rise to this thought:

"In all the immeasurable, incalculable worlds of the ten directions, all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all come to the place where the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra is located for the sake of revering the Dharma, to behold, pay homage to, listen to, and receive it."
"If they should come, I shall bestow upon them the gift of Dharma so that they may each obtain the Dharma and return. Kausika!

Wherever this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra resides, I do not merely say that the hosts of devaputras from the four great continents and the desire and form realms who abide in the bodhicitta will go to that place out of reverence for the Dharma to gaze upon it, pay homage, and receive it upon their heads.

Kauśika! Throughout the three thousandfold great thousandfold world system, among all those in the desire realm and the form realm who abide in the bodhicitta, each of these hosts of devaputras, out of reverence for the Dharma, shall go to wherever this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra is located, to behold, worship, praise, rejoice in, and receive it upon their heads.
Having paid homage and received [the teaching] upon the crown of their heads, they each returned to their respective celestial realms.

"Furthermore, Kauśika, wherever those sons or daughters of good family who uphold, read, and recite the *Prajñāpāramitā* may dwell—whether in a hall or a dwelling where this scripture is present—that place shall be firm, secure, and indestructible. There, beings of great power—gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—will constantly come to that location to hear and receive the True Dharma."
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If the assemblies of devas, nāgas, spirits, and others should come, how should those sons and daughters of good family recognize them?”
The Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!

If a son or daughter of good family who upholds this True Dharma sees a great radiance, they should know that it is the assembly of devas, nāgas, spirits, and others who have come to their location to listen to and receive the True Dharma.”

Furthermore, Kausika, if one perceives various subtle and exquisite fragrances, one should know that this sign indicates that the hosts of devas, nāgas, and spirits have come to that place. Therefore, Kausika!
Whichever place a son or daughter of good family who upholds this True Dharma resides, they should always keep their dwelling pure and clean, removing all impure and foul objects.

If those hosts of devas, nāgas, and spirits should at any time come to that place and behold these signs of purity and so forth, those devas, nāgas, and spirits will give rise to a mind of joy, delight, and happiness; meanwhile, the minor, weak-bodied spirits who previously resided there will all flee far away and depart from that house.

Why is this? Those deities, nāgas, and spirits of great power upon whom those weak spirits constantly rely, and those weak spirits who always follow the hosts of powerful deities, nāgas, and spirits, travel together to various regions.
Therefore, Kauśika, wherever this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra exists, those who uphold the Dharma should always keep that place pure and clean; for they thereby honor the Eye of the True Dharma.
Kauśika! Because these sons and daughters of good family respectfully uphold the power of the true Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā, they shall obtain great merit in this present life.
"Furthermore, Kauśika, when these sons and daughters of good family receive, uphold, and practice the Prajñāpāramitā, their bodies are free from fatigue and their minds are not indolent;
they are free from all suffering and affliction, experiencing serenity and joy, sleeping in peace and awakening with clarity."
Ananda, within his dream he beheld sublime visions: he saw the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, seated at the site of enlightenment;
or he saw the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, turning the great Wheel of Dharma;
or he saw the precious stūpas containing the relics of the Tathāgata; or he saw the assembly of śrāvakas.
Either they see the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, or they hear the proclamation of the profound sound of the Dharma of the *prajñāpāramitā*,
or they hear the proclamation of the factors of enlightenment (*bodhipākṣika-dharma*),
or again they see various bodhisattva-mahāsattvas currently realizing unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), or they see various bodhisattvas...
A bodhisattva mahāsattva upholds this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā, or hears it being proclaimed that the Prajñāpāramitā encompasses all-knowledge.
Some see Buddha-fields that are vast and pure; some hear the various Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, teaching the Dharma for bodhisattvas through skillful means.

Some see a certain Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, in a certain direction, at a certain place, and in a certain world, surrounded by a respectful assembly of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, as he teaches the Dharma.

Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family will see such sublime signs in their dreams; having awakened, their bodies and minds will be light and serene, and they will experience a sense of well-being and joy.
Having attained such satisfaction and bliss, that person does not give rise to thoughts of craving toward delicious food and drink.
It is like a bhikṣu practicing meditative cultivation who, upon arising from samādhi, does not give rise to thoughts of delicious food and drink.
Kauśika! It is the same for those sons and daughters of good family who uphold the Prajñāpāramitā. Why is this?

Because these sons and daughters of good family abide in the practice of contemplation associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they receive an increase in physical strength from devas, nāgas, spirits, and others; therefore, they do not give rise to thoughts regarding food and drink.
Kauśika! Sons and daughters of good family who uphold the Prajñāpāramitā shall obtain these merits in this present life.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family is able to merely transcribe this Prajñāpāramitā into a scroll and install it for veneration, you should know that such a person attains great merit."

How much more so for those who, desiring to seek great enlightenment, give rise to a mind of faith and understanding toward this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā, listen to it, receive it, read it, recite it, and extensively explain its meaning to others, thereby causing the True Dharma to abide long in the world.

By these causes and conditions, the Buddha-eye is uninterrupted and the True Dharma does not perish; and as the various assemblies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each uphold, proclaim, and expound it, they immediately attain the unimpaired and indestructible Dharma-eye.
Furthermore, they honored and venerated [the Buddha] by making various kinds of offerings, such as incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments.
You should know that by virtue of these causes and conditions, the merit obtained by such a person will be immeasurable and boundless.

Therefore, Kauśika, if any son of good family or daughter of good family desires to accomplish such supreme merit, they should develop a mind of faith and understanding toward this Dharma-door of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, receive, uphold, read, recite, memorize, and contemplate it; furthermore, they should explain its meaning extensively for others, and moreover, honor and revere it with various offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, and ointments.
Chapter Four: Praising Merit. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!

If one portion were the relics of the Tathāgata filling the entirety of Jambudvīpa, and another portion were this Prajñāpāramitā written as a manuscript scroll, which of these two portions would you take?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If one were to take as one portion the relics of the Tathāgata filling the entirety of Jambudvīpa, and as another portion a single scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, between these two portions, I would choose the portion of the Prajñāpāramitā.”

Why is this? Because all the transformation bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*), the bodies of ultimate reality (*bhūtārthakāya*), and the Dharma-teaching bodies (*dharmadeśanākāya*) of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas—such bodies as these are all produced from the Dharmakāya and manifest from Suchness (*tathatā*) and the Reality Limit (*bhūtakoṭi*).
That which is suchness and the limit of reality is what is called the *prajñāpāramitā*.

All the bodies of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, likewise arise from this *prajñāpāramitā*; therefore, one is able to behold, pay homage to, and make offerings to the relics (*śarīra*) of the Tathāgata.
Although one may make offerings to the relics of the Tathāgata, it is not as good as honoring and making offerings to this Prajñāpāramitā. Why is that?
Because the bodies of all Tathāgatas are born from this Prajñāpāramitā.
World-Honored One!
It is as if, for example, I were in the Sudharmā Hall among the Trāyastriṃśa gods, seated upon my throne, proclaiming the essentials of the Dharma to the sons of the gods.

Whenever I rose from that seat due to some cause or condition, there were devaputras who might come at that time; even though they did not see me, they would simply gaze upon and pay homage to my seat with reverence, circumambulate it, and then depart.
He thought to himself:
"The Lord Śakra, King of Devas, constantly proclaims the essential teachings of the Dharma for all the devas from this seat; therefore, I now pay homage to this seat."
“World-Honored One!
It is likewise with the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
All the omniscience of the Tathāgata relies upon the body of the Tathāgata, and this body, in turn, is obtained through omniscience.”

For this reason, from the knowledge of things as they truly are (yathābhūta-jñāna) arises the Tathāgata’s omniscience (sarvajña-jñāna), and that knowledge, in turn, is born from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
"Blessed One!
For this reason, between these two portions, I shall take only the portion of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Blessed One!"

It is not that I lack reverence for the relics of the Buddha; rather, because the relics of the Tathāgata are born from the *prajñāpāramitā*, I take this portion of the *prajñāpāramitā* as being equivalent to making offerings to the relics of the Tathāgata.
World-Honored One!

Setting aside these relics of the Tathāgata that would fill Jambudvīpa, whether they fill the four great continents, the small thousand-world system, or the medium thousand-world system—let all such quantities be set aside.
Suppose one portion consisted of the relics of the Tathāgata filling a trichiliocosm, and another portion consisted of this Prajñāpāramitā written as a manuscript scroll.
"Bhagavān! Between these two portions, I would take only the portion of the *prajñāpāramitā*. Bhagavān!"
It is not that I lack reverence for the relics of the Tathāgata; rather, it is because all the relics of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, are born from the Prajñāpāramitā.
The bodies of all Tathāgatas take omniscience as their support, and this very omniscience, in turn, arises from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, between these two parts, I choose only the part of the perfection of wisdom.
“World-Honored One!
It is like a great maṇi jewel, which possesses all colors and forms and has great merit; wherever it may be, non-human beings find no opportunity to harm it.”
In whatever dwelling of non-human beings there may be, if a man or a woman enters that house carrying this maṇi-jewel, those non-humans shall immediately depart from that house.
Furthermore, if a person briefly places this jewel upon their body, that person will immediately be able to pacify all matters such as evil poisons and suffering.

Moreover, if there are those afflicted by diseases such as wind, bile, phlegm, or swelling, they should place this jewel upon their bodies, and all such illnesses and sufferings will be completely eliminated.
This maṇi jewel can provide illumination in the darkness of night.
When various regions are intensely hot, this maṇi jewel can produce coolness.
When various regions are extremely cold, this maṇi-jewel can provide warmth.

When various regions are plagued by great venomous insects and the like that inflict all manner of evil poisons, if such a great maṇi-jewel is present, they will naturally depart from afar and be unable to cause harm.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who has been harmed by various venomous insects, as soon as that person sees this maṇi jewel, the poison will be instantly neutralized.

Moreover, if there is anyone afflicted with eye diseases such that they are unable to perceive external objects, if one places this jewel upon their eyes, that person will immediately be able to see clearly and be freed from all suffering and affliction.
Furthermore, if this jewel is placed in water, the jewel becomes the same color as the water.
If this jewel is placed in water of various colors—blue, yellow, red, or white—the jewel is likewise able to conform to each of those various colors and become identical to them.
Furthermore, if this jewel is placed within garments of various colors—blue, yellow, red, or white—it is also able to conform to the color of each respective garment, becoming identical to it.
If this jewel is placed in turbid water, the water immediately becomes clear of itself.
World-Honored One!
This maṇi jewel possesses such merit as these various colors and characteristics.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas:
"Regarding this great maṇi jewel which you describe as possessing all such virtues—is it a treasure belonging to the heavens?"
"Is this a treasure possessed by humans?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to Ānanda: "This is a great maṇi jewel from the heavens.

Humans of Jambudvīpa also possess such jewels, yet they rarely give rise to respect or affection for them; only the jewels of the heavens are cherished and esteemed by people, because they are endowed with all manner of excellent colors, forms, and superior qualities."

If one were to compare the jewels of Jambudvīpa with the jewels of the heavens, the former would not equal even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, a koṭi-th part, a hundred-koṭi-th part, a thousand-koṭi-th part, or a hundred-thousand-koṭi-th part; it would not equal even a calculable part, a numerical part, a fractional part, a metaphorical part, or even a part by way of *upaniṣad*.

This celestial maṇi jewel is perfect in all its characteristics; if this wondrous jewel is placed within a jeweled casket, then whenever one takes that jewel away, this jeweled casket itself will also possess all virtues and be held in reverence by people.
"Why is this? Because it is a magnificent and exquisite vessel for great and abundant jewels.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Prajñāpāramitā is likewise so.

It is fully endowed with the merit of the knowledge of all modes of knowing; thus, even after the parinirvāṇa of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, their sarīras may also be venerated, paid homage to, and offered to.”

Why is this? Because the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) relies upon the body of the Tathāgata; therefore, the relics of the Tathāgata are like that precious vessel, and the knowledge of all modes is like the treasure contained within it.
For this reason, the relics of the Tathāgata are worthy of being beheld, venerated, and offered to.
World-Honored One!
If a Buddha-Tathāgata were to proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā throughout all worlds, that would constitute the production of true offering.
If a Dharma teacher is able to expound the *prajñāpāramitā* for others, this also constitutes the production of true worship.
World-Honored One!

It is like a king’s minister who, having received the king’s command, enters among a great multitude of people without giving rise to fear, because he relies upon the power of his sovereign’s majesty and virtue.
All Dharma-preachers are likewise; they proclaim the essentials of the Dharma amidst all assemblies without giving rise to fear, because they rely on the power of the merit of the Great Dharma.
Therefore, one should honor and make offerings to the Dharma-preacher; by making offerings to the Dharma-preacher, one also makes offerings to the relics of the Tathāgata.
"World-Honored One!..."

As previously described, suppose the relics of the Tathāgata were to fill a trichiliocosm; furthermore, suppose as many trichiliocosms as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River were filled with the relics of the Tathāgata to constitute one portion, while a single scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra constituted the other portion.
"Bhagavān! Of these two portions, I too would take the portion of the Prajñāpāramitā. Bhagavān!"

It is not that I lack respect for the relics of the Tathāgata; rather, it is because the relics of the Tathāgata are born from the *prajñāpāramitā* and serve as the basis for all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), that I shall honor and make offerings to the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Therefore, World-Honored One,
if one makes offerings to this Prajñāpāramitā, it is equivalent to making offerings to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family desires to see the true bodies of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, who currently dwell and preach the Dharma in the immeasurable, incalculable worlds of the ten directions, they should practice this Prajñāpāramitā according to the Dharma, abide in it with proper correspondence, and contemplate it as it truly is."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
“So it is, so it is! Kauśika!”
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past attained the realization of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi precisely because they practiced this Prajñāpāramitā.
In future ages, all the infinite and countless Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas shall, by virtue of practicing this Prajñāpāramitā, attain the realization of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Kauśika! I, who am now the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, have likewise attained anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi by practicing this prajñāpāramitā.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This Great Pāramitā is called the Prajñāpāramitā. Because the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has cultivated this Prajñāpāramitā, he knows, as they truly are, the various mental activities of all sentient beings.”
The Buddha said, “So it is, so it is! Kausika!”
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having practiced this prajñāpāramitā throughout the long night, are able to thoroughly understand the various mental activities of all sentient beings.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How is it, World-Honored One?
Does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice only the perfection of wisdom?"
"Does he also practice the other perfections? The Buddha said, "Kauśika!"
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas all practice the six pāramitās. Furthermore, Kauśika,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice this prajñāpāramitā, it serves as the leader of all the pāramitās.

That is to say: the perfection of generosity is able to relinquish; the perfection of ethical discipline is able to protect; the perfection of patience is able to endure; the perfection of diligence is able to increase; the perfection of meditative concentration is able to abide in tranquility; and the perfection of wisdom is able to thoroughly understand all phenomena.
Because they have thoroughly understood all phenomena, they are able to guide and instruct in the various *pāramitās*, embracing them through skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*).
By means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, they dedicate [their merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and dedicate it toward the most supreme and pure *dharmadhātu*.
Kauśika! It is like the various trees in Jambudvīpa, which have diverse colors and forms, diverse trunks and stems, diverse branches and leaves, and diverse flowers and fruits.
Although they are thus each distinct, the shadows of all those trees are one and no different.
Kauśika, the various pāramitās are likewise; although they are distinct, through the skillful means of the prajñāpāramitā, they are all dedicated toward that omniscience (sarvajñatā).
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is marvelous, World-Honored One!
The Prajñāpāramitā possesses great merit; the Prajñāpāramitā possesses immeasurable merit; the Prajñāpāramitā possesses boundless merit.”
5. Chapter on Right Merit (Samyakpuṇya), Part One. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, desiring to seek great enlightenment, give rise to a mind of faith and resolve toward this Dharma-door of the Prajñāpāramitā, listen to it, receive it, read it, recite it, and even explain its meaning for others, so that this True Dharma may long abide in the world."

By these causes and conditions, they are able to ensure that the Buddha-eye is not interrupted and the True Dharma does not perish; as the various assemblies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each uphold it, the True Dharma thereby becomes indestructible and imperishable.
Furthermore, having heard it, they offer this praise:
"This Prajñāpāramitā possesses great benefit; it is of great fruit and retribution; it is fully endowed with immeasurable and vast merit; it is that which is correctly understood."

This Prajñāpāramitā is a great protection; this Prajñāpāramitā is that which is to be revered; this Prajñāpāramitā is most supreme and difficult to obtain; this Prajñāpāramitā gives rise to faith and understanding.

These sons and daughters of good family, having themselves praised, honored, and revered this Prajñāpāramitā, further perform various kinds of offerings toward it with incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, precious canopies, and exquisite garments.
Furthermore, if there are sons or daughters of good family who, with this scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, transmit it to others and cause them to make offerings to it.
“World-Honored One!
Between these good sons and good daughters, which obtains the greater merit?
The Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
“Kauśika! I shall question you; answer as you see fit. What do you think?”
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, after the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha Tathāgata, honors, reveres, and makes various offerings to his relics.
Furthermore, if there are good men or good women who, having personally made offerings to the Buddha’s relics, then transmit them to others, causing them to honor, revere, and make offerings to them.
“Among the merit obtained by such sons and daughters of good family, which would be greater?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

If a son or daughter of good family were to personally make offerings to the relics of the Tathāgata, it would not equal the merit obtained by someone who transfers those Buddha-relics to another person, enabling them to make offerings; the number of blessings gained from this is far greater.
The Buddha said: “So it is, so it is, Kauśika!”

If a son or daughter of good family were to write out this Prajñāpāramitā as a scroll and make offerings to it themselves, it would not be as meritorious as someone else writing out this Prajñāpāramitā as a scroll and transmitting it to another person so that they may make offerings to it.
By these causes and conditions, this son of good family or daughter of good family will obtain exceedingly great merit. "Furthermore, Kausika!
If there is a son of good family or daughter of good family who instructs every single sentient being throughout the entire Jambudvipa to cultivate the ten wholesome courses of action."
Kauśika! What do you think? Would that person, by reason of this cause and condition, obtain much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to the Buddha,
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! Although these sons and daughters of good family obtain much merit by this cause and condition, it is not equal to that of someone who, regarding this *prajñāpāramitā*, gives rise to a mind of faith and understanding, gives rise to the bodhicitta, and abides in the dharma of a bodhisattva; who, by means of this *prajñāpāramitā*, copies it into a scroll, receives, maintains, reads, and recites it, with a heart of joy expounding it for others, or further explaining its meaning for others, giving rise to a pure mind toward this true dharma and being free from all doubt, and further exhorting others to receive and maintain it, saying:”

“O son of good family, this Prajñāpāramitā is the path of the bodhisattva; you should train yourself therein. One who trains in this manner will be able to swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
They are able to exhaustively bring all realms of sentient beings to universal dwelling in the reality-limit of *tathatā*. Kausika,
these sons and daughters of good family will gain exceedingly great merit.
"Furthermore, Kauśika! Let alone all the sentient beings filling Jambudvīpa.
Suppose a person were to take all the sentient beings filling the four great continents and each instruct them to practice the ten wholesome courses of action; [and suppose they were to do so]..."
Setting aside that number, suppose there were as many sentient beings as fill a small thousand-world system, and each were taught to practice the ten wholesome actions;
setting aside that number as well, suppose there were as many sentient beings as fill a medium thousand-world system, and each were taught to practice the ten wholesome actions;
setting aside that number as well, suppose there were as many sentient beings as fill a great trichiliocosm, and all were taught to practice virtue.

Setting aside this number, suppose one were to teach and transform every single sentient being throughout as many trichiliocosm world systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, causing each of them to practice the ten wholesome paths of action.
Kauśika, what do you think? Would that person,
by reason of these causes and conditions, acquire much merit?
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to the Buddha,
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“Kauśika! Although these sons and daughters of good family obtain much merit by this cause and condition, it is not equal to that of someone who, regarding this *prajñāpāramitā*, gives rise to a mind of faith and understanding, gives rise to the bodhicitta, and abides in the dharma of the bodhisattvas; who copies this *prajñāpāramitā* into a scroll, receives, upholds, reads, and recites it; who generates a heart of joy and expounds it for others, or further explains its meaning for others; who generates a pure mind toward this true dharma, becomes free from all doubt and confusion, and further exhorts others to receive and uphold it, saying:”

"O son of good family, this Prajñāpāramitā is the path of the bodhisattvas; you should practice and study within it. One who studies in this manner will be able to swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi)."
They are able to exhaustively bring all realms of sentient beings to dwell universally in the reality-limit of *tathatā*. Kausika!
Such sons and daughters of good family obtain exceedingly great merit.
