Having made this offering of flowers, he joined his palms in reverence and spoke these words:
"O Bodhisattva Mahāsattva!
From this day forward, I shall serve you with my own body, attending to you and making offerings."
Having spoken thus, she descended from the air and stood before the Bodhisattva.
At that time, the daughter of the elder, together with her five hundred handmaidens, addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita, saying:

"We each offer our own bodies to you to serve and provide for you; we likewise offer these five hundred chariots. We pray that in every life we are born into, we may always plant roots of goodness together with you, always meet one another, and always draw near to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to pay them respect and make offerings."
"I offer my body; I pray that you will graciously accept it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita said to the merchant's daughter and the others:
"If you serve me with a sincere heart and comply with everything I do, then I shall accept [your offering]."
The daughters of the elder said, "We offer ourselves to you with sincere hearts; whatever you may command, we shall comply.
Then, having accepted them, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata, saying:
"Now this daughter of the elder, along with her five hundred maidservants, and even these five hundred chariots adorned with jewels, are all offered back to you.
May the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva deign to accept them."
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita,
saying: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!"
Such joyful relinquishment is exceedingly rare.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can relinquish in this manner, they will swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and master the skillful means of the prajñāpāramitā.

"Good son! When the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past were practicing the bodhisattva path in their former lives, they all practiced this very practice of relinquishment just as you do now, diligently seeking the causes and conditions for the Prajñāpāramitā; they were exactly like you now, without any difference."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata, desiring to bring to fulfillment the roots of goodness of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita, accepted the daughter of the elder and the others.
Having received it, he immediately gave it back to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata rose from his Dharma-seat in the afternoon and entered his palace.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita thought to himself:

"For the sake of seeking the Dharma, I must now apply myself with diligence; whether walking or standing, I shall wait for the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata to emerge from his palace and ascend the Dharma-seat, so that I may hear and receive this profound, true Dharma."

"At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata constantly entered the samādhi of the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) as well as immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattva samādhis; he remained within these various samādhis for seven years."

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita, for seven years, whether walking or standing, never sat or lay down; he did not think of food or drink, nor did he feel weariness, but thought only of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata: "When will he emerge from samādhi and ascend the Dharma-seat?"
"May I be granted the opportunity to hear the *prajñāpāramitā*.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita scattered various kinds of flowers upon the Dharma seat; the daughter of the elder and her five hundred female attendants likewise followed the example of the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita, and for seven years—whether walking or standing—they never sat or lay down. They did not think of food or drink, nor did they give rise to weariness, as they remained single-mindedly awaiting the Bodhisattva’s emergence from *samādhi*.
"At that time, because the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita was diligently applying himself with a mind that delights in the Dharma, he suddenly heard a voice in the air proclaiming:
'The Bodhisattva Dharmodgata shall emerge from samādhi after seven days have passed.'"

Having heard this voice from the air, the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita was filled with great joy and exultation; at the site of the Dharma seat, together with the merchant’s daughter and her five hundred handmaidens, he adorned it with various kinds of precious and pure ornaments.

At that time, the daughters of the elder and the others each removed the exquisite robes they were wearing and piled them up to form a seat, intending to have the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dharmodgata sit upon it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita walked about that place seeking water to sprinkle upon the ground.
Then all the Māras concealed every drop of water so that none remained visible. The Māras thought to themselves:

"If the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita fails to find water, he will give rise to suffering in his mind; because of this mental suffering, he will fall away from his resolve for the Way, and his roots of goodness will not increase."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita, realizing he was being concealed and obscured by the power of Māra, immediately thought to himself:
"I should now pierce my own body and draw blood to sprinkle upon the ground where the Dharma seat is located."
Why is this? Dust and filth would defile the seat upon which a Bodhisattva sits; it is not a place that should be impure.
Now, for the sake of seeking the Unsurpassed Dharma, even if I were to break my own body, what would I have to begrudge?

Furthermore, from lifetime to lifetime since the beginningless past, I have undergone bodies of birth and death and transmigrated through the various realms due to the causes and conditions of desire; thus, my efforts have been in vain and ultimately yielded no benefit. Never before have I sacrificed my own body or life for the sake of this pure Dharma; therefore, at this time, I ought to apply myself with diligence.
Having formed this thought, he immediately took up a sharp blade, pierced his own body, and drew blood to sprinkle upon the ground.

That daughter of a householder, along with her five hundred female attendants, likewise followed the example of the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita, piercing their bodies and drawing blood to sprinkle upon the ground.

That Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita, along with the merchant’s daughter and her retinue, being courageous and firm, performed these deeds; consequently, their roots of goodness increased, and those evil Māras could find no opportunity against them.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, having observed these events with his divine eye, thought to himself:

"The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita is truly marvelous; he has aroused great courage and donned the firm armor, not begrudging his own body or life. For the sake of seeking the Dharma, desiring to achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and wishing to extensively deliver all sentient beings from the suffering of saṃsāra, he has aroused such great diligence—how truly marvelous!"

After Śakra, Lord of Devas, had formed this thought, he immediately caused the ground where blood had been sprinkled to transform into red sandalwood scented water, such that for a hundred yojanas in every direction, there was the fragrance of sandalwood.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita,
saying: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!"

You have now exerted great diligence for the sake of seeking the unsurpassed Dharma; when the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past were practicing the bodhisattva path in their former lives, they were exactly like you now, without any difference.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita again thought to himself:
"When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata preaches the Dharma, I shall have no incense or flowers; with what, then, shall I make my offering?"
When Śakra, Lord of the Devas, knew what he was thinking, he immediately presented a thousand *droṇas* of celestial *mandārava* flowers to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita.
At that time, having received these flowers, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita divided them into two equal parts and first scattered one half beside his seat.

"At that time, after those seven years had passed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata emerged from samādhi, returned to the Dharma-seat, and sat upon it, surrounded with reverence by an immeasurable multitude of hundreds of thousands."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita, seeing the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata seated upon his throne, was filled with great joy, like a bhikṣu who has attained the bliss of the third dhyāna. He then took the celestial māndārava flowers previously set aside from those offered by Śakra, scattered them as an offering toward the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata, and with palms joined and a concentrated mind, listened to the profound and correct Dharma being proclaimed: the Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata, on account of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita, addressed the assembly, saying:
"You all should know!
All phenomena are equal, and the perfection of wisdom is also equal.
All phenomena are detached, and the perfection of wisdom is also detached.
All phenomena are immovable, and the perfection of wisdom is also immovable.
All phenomena are without conceptualization, and the perfection of wisdom is also without conceptualization.
All phenomena are fearless, and the perfection of wisdom is also fearless.
All phenomena are flavorless, and the perfection of wisdom is also flavorless.
All phenomena are boundless, and the perfection of wisdom is also boundless.
All phenomena are unarisen, and the perfection of wisdom is also unarisen.
All phenomena are without cessation, and the perfection of wisdom is also without cessation.
Space is boundless, and the perfection of wisdom is also boundless.
As the great ocean is boundless, so too is the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) boundless.
As Mount Sumeru is magnificent, so too is the perfection of wisdom magnificent.
Space is without discrimination, and the perfection of wisdom is also without discrimination.
Form is boundless, and the perfection of wisdom is also boundless.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are boundless; the perfection of wisdom is also boundless.
The earth element is boundless; the perfection of wisdom is also boundless.
The water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and consciousness element are boundless; likewise, the *prajñāpāramitā* is also boundless.
The dharma that is like a diamond is equal; likewise, the *prajñāpāramitā* is also equal.
All phenomena are without conceptual differentiation, and the perfection of wisdom is likewise without conceptual differentiation.
All phenomena are unattainable, and the perfection of wisdom is likewise unattainable.
All phenomena are equal and devoid of intrinsic nature; the perfection of wisdom is likewise equal and devoid of intrinsic nature.
All phenomena are indestructible; the perfection of wisdom is likewise indestructible.
"All dharmas are inconceivable, and the Prajñāpāramitā is also inconceivable.

At that time, having heard this Dharma, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita immediately attained within that assembly the samādhi of the equality of all dharmas and the samādhi of the detachment from all dharmas.
The samādhi of the immovability of all phenomena, the samādhi of the non-conceptuality of all phenomena,
the samādhi of the fearlessness of all phenomena, the samādhi of the tastelessness of all phenomena,
the samādhi of the boundlessness of all phenomena, the samādhi of the non-arising of all phenomena, and the samādhi of the non-extinction of all phenomena.
The *mudrā*, the *ākāśānantya-samādhi*, the *mahāsāgarānantya-samādhi*, the *sumeru-vyūha-samādhi*, the *ākāśāvikalpa-samādhi*, the *rūpānantya-samādhi*,
the *vedanā-saṃjñā-saṃskāra-vijñānānantya-samādhi*, and the *pṛthivīdhātvanantya-* [samādhi].
The samādhi of the infinite; the samādhis of the infinite elements of water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness;
the samādhi of the equality of the vajra-like dharma; the samādhi of non-discrimination regarding all phenomena;
the samādhi of non-apprehension regarding all phenomena; and the samādhi of the equality and lack of intrinsic nature of all phenomena.
The Ground, the Samādhi of the Indestructibility of All Dharmas, and the Samādhi of the Inconceivability of All Dharmas.

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita entered sixty thousand such gateways of samādhi. Within these samādhis, he beheld as many Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, throughout as many trichiliocosm world-systems in the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River; each was accompanied by a great assembly of bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, humans, and devas, proclaiming the Prajñāpāramitā through such names and such phrases.

Just as the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata now, surrounded by this great assembly in this very gathering, proclaims the *prajñāpāramitā* with such names and such phrases, it is exactly the same and no different.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Subhūti, saying:
"As I have explained, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita sought the Prajñāpāramitā with such various skillful means, firm diligence, and ardent striving."

That bodhisattva, having heard the *prajñāpāramitā* from the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Dharmodgata and having entered the various gateways of samādhi, upon emerging from those samādhis, immediately attained the perfection of great learning (*bahuśruta*), as deep, vast, and boundless as the great ocean. In this present life, he constantly beheld the Buddhas; in every birth throughout his successive lives in all Buddha-fields, he was never for even a single moment separated from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
Subhūti! You should know that those who seek the *prajñāpāramitā* possess such merits and benefits as these.
Therefore, within my Dharma now, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who seek the *prajñāpāramitā* should likewise seek it in this manner.
Chapter 32: Entrustment At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"You should now know that this Prajñāpāramitā is the mother of all Buddhas; it gives birth to the omniscient wisdom of all Buddhas."

Ānanda! Those who wish to practice the *prajñāpāramitā* should receive, uphold, read, recite, memorize, contemplate, and explain this profound and true Dharma to others; they should even transcribe a single sentence or a single verse and place it in a pure location, enshrining it with reverence and respect within a precious casket, making vast offerings of various kinds of gold, silver, rare jewels, incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, banners, flags, and precious canopies. At the very least, they should offer respect and worship according to their capacity, whether through a single incense stick, a single flower, a single prostration, or a single hymn of praise.
"You should know that such a person receives my teaching and is praised by me.
Ānanda! Is the Buddha not your Great Teacher?"
Ānanda said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
The Buddha is my Great Teacher!”
"I am a disciple of the Buddha. The Buddha said, "Ānanda!"

"You are now my disciple; you have served, honored, and respected me in this present life. After my parinirvāṇa, you should honor, respect, and make offerings to this profound and correct Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā. This is precisely what it means to honor and respect me; this is the greatest way to repay the Buddha's kindness."

Ānanda! I now entrust this profound and correct Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā to you. You should receive and uphold it, being careful not to forget or lose it, and you should proclaim and disseminate it so that it shall never be interrupted.
"Ānanda! You should apply yourself with diligence to assist in proclaiming this Dharma; do not become one who, at the end, severs the lineage of the Buddhas.
He exhorted him thus a second and a third time.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“As the World-Honored One has commanded, I shall receive and uphold it.
As the World-Honored One has commanded, I shall receive and uphold it.”
After he had made this request three times,
the Buddha said: "Ānanda!
You should know that for as long as this true Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā remains in the world, for that long the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, remain in the world teaching the Dharma.
Furthermore, Ānanda!

If there are sons or daughters of good family who, toward this profound and correct Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā, feel love and joy, revere it, receive, uphold, read, recite, memorize, contemplate, and explain it to others, and even write it down and honor it with offerings—know that these sons and daughters of good family will, in every life they are born into, constantly encounter the Buddhas and hear and receive the true Dharma.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Maitreya and the other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the Venerable Subhūti, the Venerable Śāriputra, the Venerable Ānanda, and the other great assembly of śrāvakas, together with Śakra, Lord of Devas, and all the world’s devas, humans, asuras, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The King of the Roaring Sound who Carves Wisdom with Syllables.
